claim: Advanced students (not experts, in the opened 1984 paper) fill a blank better when the program follows stereotyped plans than when it breaks plan-composition rules (plan-like 37/47 correct vs a small minority for unplan-like; chi-square 47.7). The Beta cell counts are garbled in the scan.
agent_test: Give the agent solved-subgoal tasks in canonical vs bent form; compare error rate and tokens with and without a plan-library hint.

claim: Plan knowledge separates experts from novices only for non-trivial plans (complex plan labels 3.7 vs 1.7 of 4; simple plans 4.0 vs 3.7 n.s.).
agent_test: Library entries should be spent on non-trivial plans only; test: add trivial-plan entries and measure token cost vs gain.

claim: Experts retrieve plans top-down when a schema exists and fall back to bottom-up plan creation on hard or unfamiliar problems; novices create more.
agent_test: Route: try retrieval first; if no library hit, switch to bottom-up growth from a focus goal. Compare with always-plan-top-down at equal tokens.

claim: Strongly expected plans cause expectation errors: experts miss deviations and distort recall toward the prototype (counter I recalled instead of J). Indirect LLM analogues exist (d01, d02) but no direct plan-like versus unplan-like test.
agent_test: Plant a deviation inside a canonical plan in tasks; measure whether the agent's retrieved-plan hint raises misses; add a simulate-the-interaction check and compare.

claim: Plan composition (merging, interleaving, delocalized plans) is a major source of novice and maintainer difficulty in the Yale-era studies; evidence is qualitative or second-hand.
agent_test: Compare agent errors on interleaved vs abutted compositions of the same subgoals.

claim: The composition-error claim does not hold universally: in a functional-first CS1 only 3 of 187 clear-structure solutions had between-task composition errors and only 5% had no plan, versus 36% with no pertinent code in Simon's C# class. Teaching style explains much of the difference.
agent_test: Do not assume composition is the weak spot of the agent; measure it first on our tasks.

claim: The structure students choose follows what they were taught (Clean First 87, Single Loop 38, Clean Multiple 43 of 187; Java arrays 50 of 51 single loop).
agent_test: Seed library with the structure the task family favours; test whether an offered structure is adopted.

claim: Switching between task-level naming and code writing goes with near-correct solutions; stuck students do not return to taught design steps.
agent_test: Force alternate plan-naming and code steps vs one-way plan-then-code at equal tokens.

claim: Language fit to the preferred plan raises correctness (52% vs 33% with a read-then-process loop); the tool should match the plan, not the plan the tool.
agent_test: Give the agent a tool whose call order matches its natural plan vs one that forces the reverse; measure errors.

claim: Writing a short numbered plan before code beats direct generation and code CoT (HumanEval Pass@1 48.1 / 53.9 / 60.3 with a model-made plan; 74.4 with a reference plan). Verified in the paper table.
agent_test: Plan-first vs direct at equal total tokens on our coding items; note the model is old (code-davinci-002).
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Planning gain grows with problem difficulty (complexity 1: 65.2 to 71.2; complexity 3: 31.1 to 50.2) and with model size; small models can lose (6.7B: 34.0 direct vs 30.1).
agent_test: Gate planning on difficulty estimate; test plan-always vs plan-if-hard.

claim: Plans written in a fixed small vocabulary (sequence, branch, loop) beat free-text CoT (60.64 vs 53.29 HumanEval, ChatGPT); dropping the structures costs 5 points, dropping IO costs 1.
agent_test: Plan slots (role, init, update, context) vs free prose at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The idea, not the code, is the bottleneck: a correct sketch makes solve rates polarize near 0% or 100%, and searching over plans beat repeated code sampling (PlanSearch pass@200 77.0 vs 60.6 best repeated sampling; pass@1 often lower).
agent_test: Spread N plans vs N code samples at equal tokens; report pass@1 as well since it can fall.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-27 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Composing and testing solved parts is what produces the gain, not the plan alone: Parsel 25.5% vs 6% for the same plans translated straight to Python (100 APPS problems).
agent_test: Same plans with and without a compose-and-test step.

claim: Reusing solved sub-modules or abstractions helps, with more for weaker models: CodeChain APPS 22.33 to 30.24 (GPT-3.5); ReGAL +11.5 on LOGO for CodeLlama-13B vs +1.3 on Date for GPT-3.5; centroid sub-modules beat random whole programs.
agent_test: Library on/off at equal tokens across two model strengths.

claim: Verified skill or workflow memory from solved tasks helps agents: Voyager (tree milestones 6 vs 92 iterations; skills only committed after success), AWM WebArena 23.5 to 35.5 (verified), but wrong induced workflows can hurt.
agent_test: Store only verified solutions; compare with unverified storage.

claim: LLMs recognize classic programming plans in student code (micro-F1 0.778 GPT-4o) and degrade gracefully with errors (0.726 vs rule-based 0.178); plan use correlates with passing (77.17% vs 61.40%).
agent_test: Use LLM plan labelling as the retrieval key; check label accuracy on our items.

claim: LLMs compose poorly as the composition graph grows; explicit skills plus a worked composition in context fixes synthetic tasks (DP 72.0 to 98.0).
agent_test: Add a worked composition example vs none, on tasks of rising depth.

claim: After a plan fails, repair is limited by self-feedback quality: GPT-4 feedback 33.30% vs human 52.60% overall; equal-budget gains from self-repair often marginal.
agent_test: Compare repair vs fresh resample at equal tokens.

claim: Plan theory is partly an artifact of notation and of control-flow-first comprehension; plans are not the only or first representation (Pennington, Gilmore and Green).
agent_test: Do not store plans only; also keep control-flow traces. Test hybrid index.

claim: Explicit plan retrieval by role (init, update, guard) is how to represent plans; plan frames have slots and two link types.
agent_test: Index library entries by role/goal vs by code text; measure retrieval hit rate.

claim: No study found that runs an LLM on the Rainfall plan-composition task and codes the structures. Only Codex on seven Rainfall wordings (average score near 50%, weak on empty input, no structure coding) was found.
agent_test: Run Rainfall variants on the agent as a first direct test.

claim: LLMs lose much of their skill when a familiar convention is changed while the task stays the same (HumanEval with 1-based indexing, GPT-4 pass@1 82.5 to 40.5), and complete code badly when the context holds a likely bug (CodeGen-2B 54.9% to 3.1%). This is indirect support for a plan-like versus unplan-like effect in models; the Soloway fill-in-the-blank task itself has not been run.
agent_test: Run a plan-like versus unplan-like fill-in on the agent with and without a retrieved plan hint; count default-value answers.

claim: Wrong or misleading hints in the prompt cost frontier models accuracy and tokens: CodeCrash average pass@1 drop 23.2% (13.8% with CoT), reasoning models 2 to 3 times the tokens on plausible wrong hints; XYEval drops up to 46.7% on five 2026 models, only partly fixed by a generic warning.
agent_test: Inject a wrong stored plan into 20 tasks; measure pass rate and tokens with and without a run-and-compare check before use.

claim: Stored solved parts need a name and a role sentence, not only code: anonymous library abstractions lowered an LLM solver's solve rate (-30.60 REGEX, -2.91 CLEVR, -11.11 LOGO) and auto-documentation restored it (+9.73, +2.27, 0.00 on LOGO where descriptions were wrong). Which retrieval key is best (role text, code, or LLM label) is not yet compared head to head.
agent_test: A/B three keys (role sentence, code text, LLM plan label) on one task set; measure retrieval hit rate and downstream pass rate.

claim: Retrieval into the prompt helps most where the model lacks knowledge and little where it already knows: ODEX-hard (rare libraries) +20.3 to +40.1 points, while DeepSeekCoder-7B did not gain on MBPP. With a strong model, expect a small gain from a plan library on tasks it already solves.
agent_test: Compare library-on versus library-off on easy and hard tiers; report the gap by tier.

claim: At equal tokens, many cheap samples with a check beat one long thought, except for code at pass@1 (NoThinking: LiveCodeBench pass@1 favors Thinking). Reasoning models already plan inside their thinking, and more effort can lower agentic scores (o1 high 29.1% at USD 1,400 against low 27.3% at 43% less cost).
agent_test: Compare plan-then-code, direct, and best-of-N at matched tokens on the agent's model; report pass@1 and pass@k.

claim: Up-front planning alone misses issues that appear during implementation; allowing thought inside the code beat up-front thinking with fewer tokens (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, average 61.0 to 70.3, no-upfront ablation only -2.8). This used training, so it is not a scaffold result.
agent_test: Allow a re-plan trigger during coding (failed test or surprise) and measure its use against plan-once.

claim: A strong model that turns a plan into code fills in the plan's missing parts, so passing tests do not prove the plan was sound (GPT-4 false positives; 12 of 13 false-positive plans scored 0 or 1 of 5, one plan scored 4/5 then 0/5 on rerun; cost over USD 200). Judge a plan with the problem statement withheld and with reruns.
agent_test: Execute stored plans from the plan text alone, three runs each; keep only those that pass at least 2 of 3.

claim: Fixation on a familiar pattern limits adaptation: novices who have seen a general approach only in one form struggle to adapt it (13 talk-alouds, 4 narratives). A library should hold more than one variant per goal. Evidence on whether explicit plan teaching changes plan choice remains absent (de Raadt not opened).
agent_test: Store two or more variants per goal and test whether the agent picks between them against task constraints.
